title: Scalar-adjoint comparisons commute with unit-preserving quotient transitions
statement: On an essentially small site J, let R, S, T be commutative ring sheaves, with maps phi: R to S and psi: R to T. Let A and B be normalized scalar models as in [lem-pur-system-scalar-model], and let Fm and Fn be other left adjoints to restriction along phi and psi. Let Xm and Xn be functors equipped with isomorphisms em: Xm to A.model.E and en: Xn to B.model.E, in the module categories of [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. Fix a base module M, a ring-sheaf map g: S to T and an equality e: restriction(g) composed with restriction(phi) equals restriction(psi). Suppose delta: Xm(M) to restriction(g)(Xn(M)) carries every local normalized unit tensor to the corresponding unit tensor under em and en. Let q: Fm(M) to restriction(g)(Fn(M)) be the canonical quotient mate of the two given adjunctions and e, as in [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Then delta followed by the restricted comparison en composed with leftAdjointUniq(B.ordinaryAdj, Fn) equals the comparison em composed with leftAdjointUniq(A.ordinaryAdj, Fm), followed by q. No flatness, surjectivity, or equality of S and T is required.

source.place: Tags 03D7 and 03EK: scalar-extension adjunction, unit tensors and the scalar Hom correspondence.

proof.text: Precompose both maps with the inverse of em. Apply scalar-extension Hom extensionality: it suffices to compare their values on every local tensor one tensor x.

The left-adjoint uniqueness isomorphism preserves adjunction units. Consequently, on a unit tensor, the left-hand composite is the unit of Fn, by the hypothesis on delta; the initial model isomorphisms cancel on the right-hand composite.

By the defining Hom transpose of the canonical quotient mate, the unit of Fm followed by restriction of q equals the unit of Fn followed by the inverse comparison e. Scalar restriction does not change section functions; the equality-transport comparison e has identity section function. Evaluating this unit equation therefore identifies the remaining right-hand value with the unit of Fn. Hom extensionality now gives the morphism equality.

theorem systemScalarTransitionComparison
    {C : Type c} [Category.{v} C] [EssentiallySmall.{r} C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})]
    {R S T : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{r}}
    (φ : R ⟶ S) (ψ : R ⟶ T)
    (A : SheafOfModules.SystemScalarModel φ) (B : SheafOfModules.SystemScalarModel ψ)
    {Fm : Mod J R ⥤ Mod J S} (am : Fm ⊣ res φ)
    {Fn : Mod J R ⥤ Mod J T} (an : Fn ⊣ res ψ)
    {Xm : Mod J R ⥤ Mod J S} {Xn : Mod J R ⥤ Mod J T}
    (em : Xm ≅ A.model.E) (en : Xn ≅ B.model.E) (M : Mod J R)
    (g : ring J S ⟶ ring J T)
    (e : SheafOfModules.restrictScalars g ⋙ res φ = res ψ)
    (δ : Xm.obj M ⟶ (SheafOfModules.restrictScalars g).obj (Xn.obj M))
    (hδ : ∀ (V : Cᵒᵖ) (x : M.val.obj V),
      (en.hom.app M).val.app V (δ.val.app V ((em.inv.app M).val.app V
        (SheafOfModules.systemModelTmul A.model M V 1 x))) =
          SheafOfModules.systemModelTmul B.model M V 1 x)
    (q : Fm.obj M ⟶ (SheafOfModules.restrictScalars g).obj (Fn.obj M))
    (hq : q = (coefficientQuotientNatTrans am an
      (SheafOfModules.restrictScalars g) (eqToIso e)).app M) :
    δ ≫ (SheafOfModules.restrictScalars g).map
      ((en ≪≫ B.ordinaryAdj.leftAdjointUniq an).hom.app M) =
        ((em ≪≫ A.ordinaryAdj.leftAdjointUniq am).hom.app M) ≫ q
